findings.title: Unchanged post-cutover cron fails on every rerun
findings.description: `production_changes()` strips new arguments from `new` but not `old`. After cron installation, rerunning the cutover compares identical post-cutover files asymmetrically and fails step 4. This also blocks recovery from later failures. Reproduced with identical inputs. Normalize both sides and add a post-install rerun test.

findings.title: Reconcile is armed without running its final verification
findings.description: The accepted prefix also matches `=== weekly backup done (unarmed)`. In `scripts/cron_weekly_backup.sh:152-155`, that outcome exits **before** the offsite mirror and final checksum check. The cutover nevertheless creates the arm file, enabling subsequent destructive reconciliation without exercising the promised verification. Execute and verify the initial reconciliation before retaining the arm file; update the test that currently treats the unarmed outcome as sufficient.

findings.title: Failed health commands can pass using stale logs
findings.description: `run_health()` ignores the command result and reads the existing log’s last line without checking that this invocation appended it. A failed command can therefore pass both health gates using an earlier clean summary. Reproduced with exit 127 and an unchanged clean log. Require fresh output while preserving the first check’s intentionally tolerated stale-backup state.

findings.title: File failures bypass the promised failure report
findings.description: `run_steps()` catches only `StepFailed` and `CalledProcessError`. Missing/unreadable logs and failed filesystem operations raise uncaught exceptions, preventing `main()` from reaching report generation. Reproduced with `FileNotFoundError`. Record filesystem failures at the process boundary and ensure report generation runs after step failures.
